
# Both-sides wrapping

This paragraph comes before the picture and stays the anchor whenever the block right after the picture cannot be one -- another image paragraph, or a heading -- so the words below keep their own separate life.

![A centred picture][opaque] <!--md-layout:v1 width=22% wrap=around x=50%-->

The picture sits at the centre of the column here, narrow enough that this long run of ordinary reading prose must wrap into lines on its left side and, further down where the picture ends, spill back out to the column edge on both sides as it clears the reserved obstacle entirely, giving the runner lines to compare on each side of the centred picture in turn.
